audience.text: Python developers building tools that parse, inspect, modify, or serialize HTML documents using WHATWG DOM APIs, CSSOM styling, and URL/encoding utilities.

capabilities.text: Parse HTML strings, bytes, fragments, and files into a DOM document using `HTMLDocument.parse`, `HTMLDocument.parse_fragment`, and `HTMLDocument.load`.
capabilities.title: Parse HTML into DOM

capabilities.text: Create, append, and mutate DOM nodes; access attributes, classes, datasets, and text content; query by ID, tag name, class, or selector helpers.
capabilities.title: DOM manipulation and querying

capabilities.text: Attach CSS stylesheets, inspect rule types, and compute final styles for elements using `get_computed_style` and `ComputedStyleDeclaration`.
capabilities.title: CSSOM styling and resolution

capabilities.text: Parse and manipulate URLs with `URL` and `URLSearchParams`; detect encoding from byte streams using `detect_encoding`.
capabilities.title: URL and encoding utilities

capabilities.text: Execute JavaScript against a parsed DOM using `JSContext` backed by QuickJS, with support for module registration and read-only DOM proxies.
capabilities.title: JavaScript execution

capabilities.text: Serialize documents, fragments, or elements to HTML strings using `serialise`, `outer_html`, or `XMLSerializer`.
capabilities.title: Serialization

capabilities.text: Drive the WHATWG-compliant tokenizer directly using `Tokenizer` and inspect tokens like `StartTagToken`, `CommentToken`, or `DoctypeToken`.
capabilities.title: Tokenizer control

capabilities.text: Build internal layout structures (`BoxNode`, `FragmentRoot`, `PageFragment`) using `skia-python` for text-run metrics, though no public rendering API is exposed yet.
capabilities.title: Layout infrastructure

limitations.text: CSS selector matching supports core Selectors Level 3 grammar; dynamic and legacy pseudo-classes raise `NotImplementedError`, and single-colon pseudo-elements are not parsed.
CSSOM base-rule stubs `CSSRule.type` and `CSSRule.css_text` are not implemented; concrete rule subclasses expose their own properties instead.
Form constraint validation (validity-state computation) and `HTMLImageElement.decode()` are present on the API surface but not yet implemented.
The library builds internal layout structures but does not expose a public API for rendering documents to an image or PDF.
JavaScript execution via `JSContext` requires the optional `quickjs` extra and exposes a read-only DOM proxy; dynamic `import()` is not implemented.
The package requires Python 3.10 or later and `skia-python` >=87.0,<145 as a runtime dependency.

problems_solved.text: Enables parsing of HTML strings, bytes, fragments, and files into a standards-compliant DOM tree using WHATWG tokenization and tree-construction algorithms.
Supports programmatic DOM manipulation, attribute access, text content updates, and querying by ID, tag name, class, or CSS selectors.
Provides CSSOM-based style resolution, including computed style calculation, stylesheet attachment, and selector matching.
Offers URL parsing, query parameter manipulation, and byte-stream encoding detection for robust handling of web resources.

product_summary.text: Aspose.HTML FOSS for Python is an open-source Python library for parsing HTML into a standards-based DOM tree, applying CSS, serializing markup, and optionally executing JavaScript via QuickJS.

uncertainties: The exact set of CSS pseudo-classes unsupported by the matcher and parser is not fully listed in the facts.
The scope of 'read-only DOM proxy' in `JSContext` is not detailed beyond `document.querySelector` and `window.getComputedStyle`.
Whether `HTMLImageElement.decode()` is stubbed or absent from the public surface is not confirmed by symbols.
The behavior of `HTMLDocument.load` for remote URLs is not specified in the examples or symbols.
The extent of `TreeWalker` and `NodeIterator` support for custom filters is not evident from available symbols.
The handling of `!important` and cascade layers in `get_computed_style` is not explicitly demonstrated.

workflows.name: Parse and modify HTML
workflows.text: Parse an HTML string using `HTMLDocument.parse`, create new elements with `Document.create_element`, append them to the DOM, and serialize the result using `serialise`.

workflows.name: Apply and resolve CSS
workflows.text: Create a `CSSStyleSheet`, attach it to a `Document`, and resolve computed styles for elements using `get_computed_style` to determine final styling.

workflows.name: Execute JavaScript against DOM
workflows.text: Wrap a `Document` in a `JSContext` and evaluate JavaScript expressions that access DOM properties like `document.querySelector` or `window.getComputedStyle`.

workflows.name: Inspect tokenizer output
workflows.text: Feed raw HTML to `Tokenizer`, call `tokenize`, and inspect tokens such as `StartTagToken` or `CommentToken` for low-level parsing control.

workflows.name: Work with URLs and query parameters
workflows.text: Construct a `URL`, modify its `search_params`, and serialize the updated URL to a string.

workflows.name: Detect character encoding
workflows.text: Pass byte data to `detect_encoding` to infer encoding, confidence, and decoded text content.
